selection_reasoning: These three tasks form a coherent multi-hop sequence in a village/structure exploration scenario. The player must first find an oak_button (typically placed on a wall or structure), which guides them to a nearby oak tree where they must mine oak_leaves. The oak_leaves task requires the player to look upward and break leaf blocks. Finally, after navigating through the area, they must find an acacia_fence_gate, which serves as a gate/exit to a fenced area. The dependency chain is: finding the oak_button on a structure orients the player toward the oak tree (spatial navigation), mining the oak_leaves clears a path or reveals the view to the acacia_fence_gate beyond. This creates a natural exploration flow where each task leads spatially to the next.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task — the player must navigate near the oak button and look toward it. The oak button is at spawn-relative (5, 2, 0) on the west wall of the cobblestone hut. max_distance=16 allows detection from a reasonable exploration range, and facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is actually looking toward the button, modeling 'the player can see the target'.

Uses count_in_box_at_most(kind='block', object='oak_leaves', max_count=17) because mining oak_leaves by hand does NOT drop the leaf block item (only shears do), so inventory_has is unreliable. Instead, we verify that at least 1 of the 18 placed oak_leaves blocks has been removed from the tree area. The generous box (X=9-15, Y=1-7, Z=-3 to 3) fully encloses the tree canopy with ±2-3 block margin. Starting count is 18; max_count=17 means at least 1 leaf was mined.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task — the player must navigate near the acacia fence gate and face it. The acacia fence gate is at spawn-relative (20, 0, -2) on the south side of the fence enclosure. max_distance=16 allows detection from a reasonable range, and facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the gate, modeling 'the player can see the target'.

scene_description: A linear east-facing exploration scene on a large cleared grass platform. The player spawns facing east toward a cobblestone hut with an oak button on its west wall. Beyond the hut (at X=12) stands a placed oak tree with leaves at Y=3-5. Further east (X=19-21) is an acacia fence enclosure with a fence gate on its south side. A cobblestone ground path runs east along Z=0 to guide the player through all three objectives sequentially.
task_text: Walk east along the path. First, find the oak button on the cobblestone structure's wall. Then continue east to the oak tree and mine some of its leaves. Finally, continue east to find the acacia fence gate on the fenced enclosure.
design_notes: Linear east-facing layout: spawn(0,1,0) → cobblestone hut with oak button(5,2,0) → oak tree(12,0-5,0) → acacia fence gate(20,0,-2). Cobblestone ground path at Y=-1 along Z=0 guides the player. Large 38x30 cleared area prevents natural terrain interference. Oak leaves are at Y=3-4 (reachable with jump-mining from ground). The oak button faces west so it's visible when approaching from the spawn direction. The acacia fence gate faces south on the south wall of the enclosure.
